articles.title: India's Data-Centre Pipeline Just Hit 8.33 Gigawatts. The Real Bottleneck Is Power, Not Demand.
articles.excerpt: A new Knight Frank tally puts India's planned data-centre capacity at five times what is live today, as hyperscalers and AI workloads pour into Mumbai and Hyderabad. For NRIs, it is a rare infrastructure bet hiding in plain sight.
articles.image_caption: Server racks and networking equipment inside a modern data centre
articles.nri_angle: Indian-American engineers and NRI investors weighing where the next decade of cloud and AI infrastructure money flows now have a concrete number: India's data-centre build-out is one of the largest in the world, and the talent and capital to run it will increasingly be sourced from the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Carmakers Just Got a Duty-Free Lane Into Britain's EV Market. The Fine Print Is a 15-Year Wait.
articles.excerpt: The India-UK trade pact opens a quota-based, duty-free path for made-in-India electric cars from Tata, Maruti and Mahindra — but the concessions phase in slowly, and the diaspora is the obvious first customer.
articles.image_caption: A Tata electric car on an Indian road
articles.nri_angle: For the large Indian community in Britain, a made-in-India electric SUV arriving duty-free is both a consumer story and a point of pride — and for NRI investors tracking Tata Motors and Mahindra, it reframes the India-UK FTA as an auto-export thesis, not just a trade headline.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Digital Fraud Rate Is Now Nearly Double the World's. The Weak Point Is the Account You Already Have.
articles.excerpt: A new TransUnion report pegs India's suspected digital fraud rate at 7.1% versus a 3.8% global average, with account takeovers surging. For NRIs running money across two countries, the exposure is doubled.
articles.image_caption: A person typing on a laptop, illustrating digital fraud and account-takeover risk
articles.nri_angle: NRIs juggle Indian bank accounts, UPI apps, brokerage logins and remittance services from abroad — a fragmented footprint that account-takeover fraudsters love, making India's spiking fraud rate a direct personal-security problem for the diaspora, not a distant statistic.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Accenture Lost a Fifth of Its Value in a Day. The Tremor Is Already Reaching Bengaluru and New Jersey.
articles.excerpt: The consulting giant's worst single-day fall ever was triggered by softening demand and the fear that AI is eating billable hours. For the Indians who staff the IT-services machine, the read-across to TCS, Infosys and Cognizant is the real story.
articles.image_caption: Accenture's shares suffered their worst single-day drop on record after weak bookings and a lowered forecast
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin technologists are the backbone of the global IT-services trade — in Accenture's and Cognizant's American offices on H-1B visas, in the Bengaluru, Hyderabad and Pune delivery centres that feed them, and in the Indian-listed giants TCS, Infosys and Wipro that report results in July. When the sector's bellwether warns of weakening demand, it is their job security and their next visa renewal on the line.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Judge Killed Trump's $100,000 H-1B Fee. Four Days Later, It Was Back. Welcome to the Whiplash.
articles.excerpt: A Boston court vacated the six-figure visa charge as an unlawful tax — then paused its own ruling pending appeal. For the Indian engineers and students who make up most of the H-1B pool, the lesson is that the uncertainty itself has become the policy.
articles.image_caption: The fate of the $100,000 H-1B fee now rests with a federal appeals court in Boston
articles.nri_angle: Indians account for roughly 71% of approved H-1B visas — the single largest group by far — so any swing in the program's cost or legality lands hardest on Indian engineers, doctors and graduate students. The on-again, off-again fight over a $100,000 fee has turned career and family planning into a guessing game for the very people the diaspora pipeline depends on.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: ISRO Bet Its Reputation on a Reliable Rocket. After Two Failures, the Workhorse Flies Again Within Days.
articles.excerpt: The PSLV — the launcher that built India's commercial space business — returns to the pad in late June after back-to-back failures rattled foreign customers. For diaspora investors in NewSpace, the stakes are credibility.
articles.image_caption: A Polar Satellite Launch Vehicle lifts off from the Satish Dhawan Space Centre at Sriharikota.
articles.nri_angle: NRIs increasingly back India's private space startups and watch ISRO's launch reliability as the bedrock that makes those investments — and India's pitch as a low-cost launch hub — credible.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Won't Legalize Crypto, but It Just Made the Paperwork Punishing. NRIs With Wallets, Take Note.
articles.excerpt: New penalties under the Income-tax Act took effect in April, and exchanges are scrambling to automate compliance. The 30% tax and 1% TDS aren't going anywhere — and the reporting net is tightening around anyone with an Indian tax footprint.
articles.image_caption: India taxes gains from cryptocurrencies and other virtual digital assets at a flat 30 percent (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who trade crypto or hold Indian wallets face a flat 30% tax, 1% TDS and now stiff reporting penalties — a compliance burden that quietly shapes whether the diaspora keeps its digital assets onshore or offshore.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Every Tech Boss Says AI Will Gut Entry-Level Jobs. The CEO Who Employs 350,000 People Is Hiring 20,000 Graduates Anyway.
articles.excerpt: Cognizant's Ravi Kumar S. is betting against the doom consensus — and the bet runs straight through India's campuses, where the company plans 20,000 fresh hires in 2026 even as it restructures.
articles.image_caption: Cognizant, whose CEO Ravi Kumar S. says fears that AI will gut entry-level tech jobs are overblown (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Cognizant is one of the largest employers of Indian tech graduates and a major H-1B sponsor; its contrarian hiring bet directly shapes the career ladder that funnels Indian engineers toward the diaspora.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Razorpay Filed for Its IPO at a $2 Billion Discount. The Markdown Is the Story.
articles.excerpt: India's biggest payments unicorn is going public at $5-6 billion, well below its 2021 peak — and the reverse-flip home tells the diaspora how the startup playbook has changed.
articles.image_caption: Razorpay, the Bengaluru fintech that has filed for its IPO (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who send money home, run India-facing businesses, or invest via GIFT City have a direct stake in Razorpay's listing — and the reverse-flip from the US rewrites the build-in-Delaware advice that guided a generation of diaspora founders.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ather's Stock Fell When It Raised ₹2,500 Crore. The CEO's One-Line Post Explains Why It Shouldn't Have.
articles.excerpt: India's third-largest electric scooter maker is running its factory at 90% and raising capital to go mass-market — a clean test case for diaspora investors weighing India's EV decade.
articles.image_caption: The Ather Energy logo; the EV maker raised Rs 2,500 crore via a qualified institutional placement (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Ather is a rare listed pure-play on Indian EV manufacturing that NRIs can actually own, and its FCCB-laced raise taps the foreign capital and returning battery talent that connect Silicon Valley to India's mobility build-out.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DoorDash Built a Chatbot That Orders Your Dinner. The Engineers Who Built It Tell a Bigger Story.
articles.excerpt: 'Ask DoorDash' is the latest gig-economy app to bolt on an AI agent — part of a costly platform rebuild overseen by an Indian-origin finance chief, and a preview of where consumer tech jobs are heading.
articles.image_caption: An autonomous food-delivery robot — delivery platforms are racing to automate ordering and fulfilment with AI
articles.nri_angle: DoorDash, Uber, Instacart and their peers employ large cohorts of Indian engineers — many on H-1B and OPT — and their pivot to agentic AI, led at DoorDash by CFO Ravi Inukonda, reshapes both the product these workers build and the security of the jobs that build it.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Salesforce Just Paid $3.6 Billion for an AI It Already Sells. Its Own Engineers Are Paying a Different Price.
articles.excerpt: Marc Benioff bought a customer-service agent startup to bolster Agentforce — days after a third round of layoffs and a record 11-day stock slide. For the Indians who staff its cloud, the math is unsettling.
articles.image_caption: Salesforce chief executive Marc Benioff, whose company is spending billions on AI agents even as it cuts staff
articles.nri_angle: Salesforce employs thousands of Indian engineers on H-1B visas across San Francisco, Hyderabad and Bengaluru; as the company spends billions on AI agents while cutting Agentforce-adjacent roles, those workers face the sharpest version of the industry's automate-or-be-automated bind.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Insurance Salesman Just Went Public. Turtlemint's Muted Debut Is a Warning for the IPO Class of 2026.
articles.excerpt: The Mumbai insurtech raised ₹883 crore at a ₹4,500 crore valuation — but a near-zero grey-market premium and a 19% wider loss tell NRI investors to read past the hype.
articles.image_caption: The Bombay Stock Exchange in Mumbai, where Turtlemint is set to list on June 29
articles.nri_angle: NRIs chasing exposure to India's fintech boom — many through the same broking apps now lining up to list — get a real-time stress test in Turtlemint: a loss-making distributor priced richly against a profitable peer, debuting into investor caution rather than euphoria.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Shipped a Chip of Its Own. It Powers an Electricity Meter, and That's the Point.
articles.excerpt: Cyient-backed Azimuth AI is rolling out ARKA GKT-1, a homegrown 40nm system-on-chip whose IP stays in India. For the diaspora's semiconductor engineers, it's the anchor that's been missing.
articles.image_caption: A silicon wafer, the foundation of semiconductor manufacturing. India's ARKA GKT-1 is designed and IP-owned domestically, though still fabricated overseas.
articles.nri_angle: The global chip industry runs on Indian engineers who left because there was nothing to build at home; a startup that designs, owns and sells its own IP in India is the kind of anchor that can begin reversing that talent and investment flow.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: 75,000 Firewalls, One Stolen Password at a Time: Why India Was Among the Worst Hit by 'FortiBleed'
articles.excerpt: The year's biggest breach exploited no new flaw, just credentials the attackers already had. India's exposed, fast-growing digital infrastructure put it near the front of the casualty list.
articles.image_caption: Rows of servers in a data center. The FortiBleed campaign compromised credentials on roughly 75,000 firewall and VPN devices worldwide.
articles.nri_angle: India's IT giants and the GCCs that multinationals run there depend on exactly this kind of gear, and many of the engineers securing Fortune 500 firms are Indian; a breach at an Accenture or Oracle ripples through diaspora-staffed teams and family businesses back home.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A UiPath Veteran Just Joined Trupeer AI. It's a Familiar Move in the India-US Tech Playbook.
articles.excerpt: Raghu Subramanian, who scaled UiPath into a $35 billion company, is betting a young Indian startup can sell AI-ready knowledge to the world's enterprises and the GCCs doing their real work.
articles.image_caption: A coworking office in Gurgaon; Trupeer AI builds a workflow knowledge layer for teams and AI agents (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Trupeer naming global capability centers as a core market points to where tech value is migrating, toward the India-based hubs absorbing engineers shaken loose by Western layoffs, sold by a diaspora operator fluent in both Silicon Valley's machinery and India's engineering depth.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adobe Is Giving Its Software Away. Shantanu Narayen's Parting Bet Is a 90-Million-User Gamble.
articles.excerpt: On his way out after 18 years, Adobe's CEO paused Creative Cloud price hikes and went all-in on freemium AI. The diaspora's engineers and creators are watching where the budget flows.
articles.image_caption: Shantanu Narayen, chairman and CEO of Adobe Inc., who is leaning into freemium AI products on his way out after 18 years.
articles.nri_angle: Adobe is a major employer of Indian engineers and a core tool for the diaspora's creators and founders; a free-first AI strategy reshapes what gets built, who gets hired, and the cost of starting a content business.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An IIT Madras Engineer Just Raised $27 Million to Make AI Prove It's Right
articles.excerpt: Pramaana Labs, led by Khosla Ventures, is betting the next AI bottleneck isn't fluency but accountability. The founder and the backers are a map of the India-US tech corridor.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons (CC)
articles.nri_angle: A diaspora founder, ex-Google and IIT Madras, backed by India-US venture firms, is building 'verifiable AI' — exactly the hard, defensible skill that protects Indian engineers as AI hollows out middle-tier coding roles.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Meta's AI Dream Job Has Turned 'Soul-Crushing.' For Indians on H-1B, Quitting Isn't an Option.
articles.excerpt: Drudgery, a keyboard-monitoring petition and a no-more-layoffs pledge expose a two-tier workforce — where citizens can walk and visa holders can't.
articles.image_caption: Meta's headquarters in Menlo Park, California, where AI teams are reporting 'soul-crushing' working conditions.
articles.nri_angle: Indians are ~72% of H-1B holders and fill Meta's engineering ranks; a morale crisis hits them differently because the 60-day visa clock turns 'I'd quit' into 'I can't leave.'
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Sees a Million Empty Chip Jobs. Its Minister Wants Indian Graduates to Fill Them — Worldwide.
articles.excerpt: Ashwini Vaishnaw says the global semiconductor industry is short a million skilled workers by 2032. For NRIs in the chip business, that is a hiring market about to tilt their way.
articles.image_caption: Union Electronics and IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw, who oversees India's semiconductor mission.
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers already staff the design floors at Nvidia, AMD, Qualcomm and Micron; a structural global talent crunch hands them leverage on pay and mobility just as India builds its own pipeline to feed the same shortage.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Wipro Just Opened a Claude Lab in Bengaluru and Promised to Retrain 10,000 People. It Is Also Admitting What AI Does to Its Old Model.
articles.excerpt: The IT giant is building a Center of Excellence around Anthropic's AI even as analysts warn the same technology is eating into the labour-heavy business that employs hundreds of thousands of Indians.
articles.image_caption: Wikimedia Commons / Wikipedia (CC)
articles.nri_angle: The Indian IT services giants are the career ladder that brought a generation of NRIs to the US on H-1B and L-1 visas; their scramble to retrain around AI signals which skills will still earn that ticket — and which won't.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: HCLTech Just Bought a Slice of India's Sovereign-AI Dream for $150 Million. The Buyer List Tells You Where the Money Now Flows.
articles.excerpt: The IT major took a 10.5% stake in Sarvam AI at a $1.5 billion valuation, betting that 'made-in-India' models for regulated industries are the next export — not cheap code.
articles.image_caption: HCLTech's campus in Noida; the IT firm is investing in India's sovereign-AI push
articles.nri_angle: NRI investors hunting India exposure beyond Flipkart and Swiggy now have a sovereign-AI thesis to track; HCLTech's bet signals which Indian deep-tech names the smart money — Bessemer, Khosla, Peak XV — is backing.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Just Lost Two of Its AI Crown Jewels in 48 Hours. Sundar Pichai's Real Problem Is Retention.
articles.excerpt: Gemini co-lead Noam Shazeer left for OpenAI and a Nobel laureate decamped to Anthropic — a brain drain that runs straight through the diaspora-heavy teams Pichai built.
articles.image_caption: Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai, photographed in 2023
articles.nri_angle: Indian engineers make up much of Google's AI workforce, and a star exodus reshapes where stability, equity upside and promotion ladders sit for diaspora professionals on H-1B status.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Everyone Is Betting on AI Chips. Arvind Krishna Just Bet $10 Billion That IBM Wins With Quantum.
articles.excerpt: IBM's Indian-American CEO says fault-tolerant quantum computing arrives by 2029 — and is staking the company's relevance, and a slice of U.S. tech strategy, on getting there first.
articles.image_caption: IBM Chairman and CEO Arvind Krishna, photographed in 2025
articles.nri_angle: Arvind Krishna is steering a piece of U.S. national tech strategy, and quantum is one of the few frontiers where the talent pool is still forming rather than being automated — a scarcity bet for diaspora engineers.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: America Restricted Its Best AI Models. India's Answer Is a Scramble to Build Its Own.
articles.excerpt: At the G7, Modi called frontier AI a 'global public good.' Back home, $234 million flowed into a new sovereign-AI unicorn — a shift NRIs should read closely.
articles.image_caption: Indian Prime Minister Narendra Modi, official portrait
articles.nri_angle: Sovereign AI changes the return-to-India calculus for diaspora engineers and opens an emerging investment class for NRIs — but the 'sovereign' label can outrun revenue, so the fine print matters.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Micron Heads Into Earnings With a Memory Shortage So Tight Even Apple Is Flinching
articles.excerpt: Sanjay Mehrotra's company has become the AI boom's quiet kingmaker. For NRIs, the story runs from a Gujarat fab to the price of the next iPhone.
articles.image_caption: Micron Technology chief executive Sanjay Mehrotra, photographed in 2025
articles.nri_angle: Micron's Indian-origin CEO is building a $2.75 billion assembly plant in Gujarat, and the same memory crunch lifting his stock is about to raise prices on every device Indian American families buy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tim Cook Says Apple's Price Hikes Are 'Unavoidable.' His Successor Inherits the Bill.
articles.excerpt: A memory-chip crunch is forcing Apple to raise prices just as John Ternus prepares to take over in September — and Indian American buyers will feel it first.
articles.image_caption: Apple chief executive Tim Cook, who steps down on September 1, 2026
articles.nri_angle: Apple devices are aspirational status objects in many Indian American homes, and a memory-driven price hike of up to $270 on the next iPhone lands just as a longtime hardware engineer takes the CEO seat.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Court Backs the Telegram Ban. For 150 Million Users, the Precedent Is the Real Story.
articles.excerpt: A Delhi court upheld a temporary block of Telegram over a medical-exam leak — handing Modi's government a powerful new tool and unsettling a diaspora that lives on the app.
articles.image_caption: The Telegram app icon displayed on a smartphone screen
articles.nri_angle: Telegram is a lifeline for NRIs coordinating family groups, community networks and business across borders; a court endorsing a government shutdown of an entire platform raises the stakes for everyone who relies on Indian internet access.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Qualcomm Is Reportedly Spending $10 Billion to Finally Crash Nvidia's Party
articles.excerpt: The Snapdragon maker is in talks to buy AI-chip startup Tenstorrent days before an investor day where it will lay out a data-centre plan. For the Indian engineers who power Qualcomm, the pivot is personal.
articles.image_caption: Qualcomm's headquarters in La Jolla, California; the chipmaker is reportedly spending $10 billion to challenge Nvidia (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Qualcomm employs thousands of Indian engineers across Hyderabad, Bengaluru and San Diego; its bet to leap from phone chips into AI data-centre silicon decides what those engineers build next — and whether India's chip-design talent gets a seat at the AI hardware table.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India's Chip Bet Has a Quiet Winner: A Bengaluru Startup Making the 'Power Brain' for AI Data Centres
articles.excerpt: Peak XV just led a $15 million round into C2i, which builds the power-delivery silicon that keeps GPUs alive. It is the part of India's semiconductor story that doesn't need a billion-dollar fab.
articles.image_caption: A silicon wafer; Bengaluru startup C2i is designing power-management chips for AI data centres (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's semiconductor mission is mostly about design IP, not fabs — and design-led startups like C2i are where NRI investors and returning engineers can actually get exposure to the chip story without waiting a decade for a factory.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tech's 2026 Layoffs Just Passed 183,000. For Indians on H-1B, the Real Clock Is 60 Days.
articles.excerpt: The cuts aren't a recession — they're an AI restructuring. And no group is more exposed to the fallout than Indian visa holders.
articles.image_caption: Silicon Valley, epicentre of the 2026 tech layoff wave now topping 183,000 jobs (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indians hold the largest share of H-1B visas, and a layoff triggers a brutal 60-day deadline to find a new sponsor or leave the US — making the 2026 AI-driven cuts an existential threat, not just a career setback.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Switched On UPI in a Nice Department Store. It's Now in Nine Countries — and That's the Point.
articles.excerpt: India's homegrown payment rail is becoming an export of soft power. For NRIs, it's both a travel perk and a tell on where Indian fintech is headed.
articles.image_caption: UPI payments are now accepted in nine countries (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: UPI's overseas rollout means NRIs can soon pay abroad with their home apps — but it's also a leading indicator for Indian fintech firms like Razorpay and PhonePe now lining up IPOs that diaspora investors can access.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: One in Five ChatGPT Users Is Now Indian. OpenAI Just Told the World Where Its Future Is.
articles.excerpt: India makes up 20% of ChatGPT's billion users — and OpenAI is pouring data centers and Tata partnerships into the market. The diaspora sits on both sides of the trade.
articles.image_caption: OpenAI CEO Sam Altman, who has called India the company's fastest-growing market
articles.nri_angle: India is becoming OpenAI's largest market, drawing data-center investment and enterprise deals that make it a serious place to build — even as the same AI boom threatens the IT-services jobs that employ much of the diaspora's network.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Just Minted Its First Space Unicorn. The Money Came From Singapore, BlackRock — and the Founders of Swiggy.
articles.excerpt: Skyroot's $60 million round crowns a Hyderabad rocket startup at a $1.1 billion valuation. For NRIs who grew up watching ISRO from the sidelines, private Indian space is now an asset class.
articles.image_caption: India's booming private space sector has produced its first unicorn (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: India's first billion-dollar private space company gives NRI investors and engineers a credible on-ramp into a deep-tech sector that was, until five years ago, entirely closed to anyone outside the government.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: TCS Just Opened India's First Oracle AI Lab. The Company That Sold Cheap Labor Is Trying to Sell Intelligence Instead.
articles.excerpt: A new Kolkata center, with four more planned, signals how India's biggest IT firm wants to survive an AI shift that is gutting its old headcount-driven model — the one that put millions of Indians on H-1B visas.
articles.image_caption: Tata Consultancy Services, which has opened India's first Oracle AI lab (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: The pyramid model that staffed thousands of Indian engineers onto H-1B and L-1 visas is being hollowed out by AI; TCS's pivot to AI 'centers of excellence' shows what the diaspora's oldest career ladder is mutating into.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A US Cybersecurity Firm Just Opened in Bengaluru and Said the Quiet Part Out Loud: It Came for the Talent, Not the Discount.
articles.excerpt: N-able's new India center, and a GCC workforce headed toward 2.36 million, mark a turning point — global firms now build core tech in India because of who is there, not because it is cheap.
articles.image_caption: University of Michigan's Ford School via flickr (BY-ND)
articles.nri_angle: As US firms move core engineering — not just support — into India captive centers for the talent, the calculus for NRIs weighing a return home shifts: the best jobs are no longer only in Silicon Valley.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Vinod Khosla Says India's $200 Billion IT Industry 'Will Be Gone.' The Diaspora's Oldest Career Ladder Is Wobbling.
articles.excerpt: The Silicon Valley investor's warning landed the same week Accenture cratered and Infosys and Wipro shares tumbled — and it hits the exact path many NRIs took to America.
articles.image_caption: Vinod Khosla, Sun Microsystems co-founder and venture capitalist, speaking at SXSW in 2024.
articles.nri_angle: The TCS-to-H-1B-to-green-card pipeline was the classic NRI on-ramp to America; Khosla's warning that AI agents will gut Indian IT threatens both the careers of family back home and the portfolios of diaspora investors betting on Indian tech.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Tesla Opened Its Fifth India Showroom in a Tech Hub Full of Future NRIs. The Price Tag Tells You Who It's Really For.
articles.excerpt: The new Hyderabad Experience Center sells a Model Y for around $61,000 — far above its US price — as Tesla tests Indian demand without yet building a factory.
articles.image_caption: A Tesla Model Y; the company opened its fifth India showroom as it courts affluent urban buyers
articles.nri_angle: NRIs who bought a Model Y in California for under $50,000 are now watching family in Hyderabad get quoted $61,000-plus for the same car — a vivid example of import-duty arbitrage and a live issue in US-India trade talks Tesla investors are tracking.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: India Will Build a Quarter of the World's iPhones This Year. A Pollution Notice Shows How Hard the Climb Still Is.
articles.excerpt: Apple's bet to diversify out of China is working — but a Tata factory notice, recalled Foxconn engineers and a steep supplier learning curve reveal the growing pains behind the headline.
articles.image_caption: Nick Kenrick.. via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: Apple's Tamil Nadu and Karnataka plants are reshaping the hometown economies of millions of NRIs' families, turning the 'India rising' story into tangible skilled-manufacturing jobs — and a live bet for diaspora investors on whether India moves beyond final assembly.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Ambani Just Priced India's Biggest IPO Ever. Two American Tech Giants Are Already Inside Jio.
articles.excerpt: Reliance filed Jio Platforms' draft prospectus Friday, targeting a record $3.8 billion — and NRIs holding any S&P 500 fund already own a sliver of it through Meta and Google.
articles.image_caption: Mukesh Ambani, whose Reliance has priced India's biggest-ever IPO for Jio
articles.nri_angle: Jio's record IPO is the cleanest direct route yet for NRIs to own India's largest digital business — but it arrives in a soft Sensex with rupee and timing risk to weigh.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: A Canadian Pension Fund Just Bet $1 Billion on India's AI Plumbing. The Diaspora Builds Both Ends of It.
articles.excerpt: CPP Investments is backing Hyderabad's CtrlS Datacenters to scale tenfold — a sign global capital sees India's AI demand as real, not speculative.
articles.image_caption: calix via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: India's AI infrastructure is being financed by global pension capital and built by Indian operators, with much of the cloud engineering routed through NRI-heavy teams in Hyderabad and Bengaluru.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: BigBasket Just Hired an Amazon Veteran to Save It. The Company That Invented Indian Grocery Is Now the Underdog.
articles.excerpt: Tata handed the CEO job to ex-Amazon executive Amit Nanda as losses widened 46% and 10-minute rivals Blinkit, Zepto and Instamart pulled ahead.
articles.image_caption: Packed grocery delivery orders ready for dispatch, as India's quick-commerce race intensifies
articles.nri_angle: BigBasket is the pipeline many NRIs use to supply aging parents in India, so a leadership shake-up amid the quick-commerce squeeze is a daily-life signal as much as an investing one.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Google Put Gemini in a $99 Speaker. The Real Target Is the Phone in Every Indian Pocket.
articles.excerpt: Sundar Pichai is smuggling his AI into the devices people already own — and India is the test bed, not the afterthought.
articles.image_caption: Alphabet and Google CEO Sundar Pichai, who is steering the company's Gemini-everywhere strategy.
articles.nri_angle: Indian Americans sit on both sides of this launch — as the engineers inside Alphabet whose teams live or die by Gemini, and as NRIs whose families in India are Google's first test market for its AI-everywhere strategy.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Nvidia's Biggest Threat Isn't a Rival. It's the Customers Now Selling Their Own Chips.
articles.excerpt: Amazon and Google are pushing custom AI silicon into the open market — and Indian engineers are building hardware on every side of the fight.
articles.image_caption: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang; the chipmaker's biggest customers are now designing their own AI silicon (Wikimedia Commons)
articles.nri_angle: Indian-origin engineers staff the silicon, memory, networking, and security layers of the AI stack at once, so the breakup of Nvidia's monopoly directly shapes diaspora careers and NRI investment portfolios.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Satya Nadella Warned Against AI Monopolies. Days Later He Started Charging by the Task.
articles.excerpt: Microsoft's new usage-based Copilot agents reveal where the most valuable work is heading — and what it means for the Indians who do so much of it.
articles.image_caption: Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella, who is reshaping Copilot around autonomous, usage-billed AI agents.
articles.nri_angle: Microsoft's pivot to billing for autonomous AI work hits the structured, multi-step knowledge tasks that Indian engineers and IT-services firms built their economic model on, redrawing which careers survive.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Accenture's Stock Just Cratered to a 7-Year Low. The Company That Employs the Most Indians Is Flashing a Warning.
articles.excerpt: Bookings shrank, AI clients are stalling at the pilot stage, and the firm has stopped breaking out its AI revenue. For Indian engineers, the world's biggest consultancy is the canary in the coal mine.
articles.image_caption: Accenture chair and CEO Julie Sweet speaking at the World Economic Forum
articles.nri_angle: Accenture employs more Indians than any other firm on earth; its stalling bookings and AI-driven caution are an early signal for the hundreds of thousands of Indian engineers whose careers run through global IT services.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: An American Manufacturer Is Teaming With Adani to Build India's AI Backbone. The Diaspora Should Watch Where the Racks Get Made.
articles.excerpt: Jabil and the Adani Group plan a vertically integrated factory for AI data-center hardware in India — racks, cooling, power — chasing a market they peg at over $3 trillion. It is the unglamorous half of the AI boom, and India wants it.
articles.image_caption: The Rick Smith Show via flickr (BY)
articles.nri_angle: For NRIs weighing whether India can move up the AI value chain beyond software services, a US-India factory making the physical hardware of data centers is the most concrete test yet of the 'build it at home' thesis.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: DeepSeek Just Raised $7.4 Billion to Stay Chinese. India's AI Startups Are Watching the Playbook Closely.
articles.excerpt: The lab that rattled Silicon Valley took outside money for the first time — through a structure designed so its founder never loses control. For India's sovereign-AI push and the diaspora that funds it, it is a lesson in how to scale without selling out.
articles.image_caption: Jwz1000520 via wikimedia (CC0)
articles.nri_angle: DeepSeek's founder-control funding model is a template India's own AI champions — and the NRI investors backing them — are studying as they try to build sovereign AI without ceding control to foreign capital.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: The Men Who Run Microsoft and Google Just Bought a Piece of Lord's. The Buyer's List Reads Like an NRI Yearbook.
articles.excerpt: A consortium led by Palo Alto Networks' Nikesh Arora — with Satya Nadella, Sundar Pichai and Shantanu Narayen — paid roughly £195 million for 49% of London Spirit, outbidding an IPL billionaire.
articles.image_caption: Palo Alto Networks CEO Nikesh Arora, who led the consortium that bought a 49% stake in London Spirit.
articles.nri_angle: Four of the most powerful Indian-origin executives in global tech just turned their personal wealth toward cricket at Lord's — a vivid sign of where diaspora capital and cultural identity are converging.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk

articles.title: Adobe Is Giving Its AI Away for Free. Shantanu Narayen Is Betting the Crowd Comes Back to Pay.
articles.excerpt: On its Q2 call, Adobe paused Creative Cloud price hikes and pushed free versions of its AI tools — freemium users jumped to 90 million — and raised full-year guidance even as the strategy squeezes near-term revenue.
articles.image_caption: Adobe chairman and CEO Shantanu Narayen, who is steering the company through its AI transition.
articles.nri_angle: Adobe under Indian-origin CEO Shantanu Narayen is a core holding for many NRI investors and a major employer of Indian engineers — its bet to give AI away and chase scale over margin is a wager the whole diaspora-heavy software sector is now making.
articles.author: Diaspora Desk
